Create OpenAlex collections from queries

Source: R/pro_collection.R
pro_collection.Rd

Turns each query into an OpenAlex collection: a saved set of IDs on OpenAlex's servers that can be reused in later queries (pro_query(collection = "col_...")) and combined with other collections. OpenAlex runs the query itself (an import); pro_collection() waits for it and then downloads what select asks for.

Usage

pro_collection(
  query_url,
  name = NULL,
  project_folder,
  select = "id",
  refresh = FALSE,
  api_key = pro_api_key(),
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

query_url

A query from pro_query(), or a named (nested) list of queries: each element becomes its own collection, named after its list names (nested names joined with _). A list of chunks from pro_query() would give one collection per chunk; use pro_query(..., chunk_limit = 1e6) to keep one query in one URL (the import has no URL length limit).

name

Name of the collection (and of its folder) for a single query. For a list, the list names are used and name must be NULL.

project_folder

Directory for the <name>.collection folders.

select

What to download: "id" (default) the member IDs only; NULL nothing; "all" the full records; or a character vector of fields (see opt_select_fields()) for records with those fields. The member IDs are downloaded whenever select is not NULL.

refresh

If TRUE, import an unchanged query again and re-download.

api_key

A personal OpenAlex API key.

verbose

Print the collection ID(s).

progress

Show the steps and import progress.

...

Passed to pro_fetch() when records are downloaded (e.g. workers, compact_parquet).

Value

Invisibly, the path of the .collection folder, or a named character vector of paths for a list of queries.

Details

Each query gets a folder <project_folder>/<name>.collection/ with

_collection.json

the query (URL, OQL, OQO), the collection (collection_id, display_name, entity_type, member_count, ...), each import, the credits used and the select that was downloaded.

_query_oql.txt, _query_oql.html

the query in readable OQL.

members/parquet/

the member IDs (id, added_at).

records/

the records when select asks for more than id (the pro_fetch() layout).

Running it again with the same project_folder and name:

  • Same query: the collection is kept (same ID). An import still running (e.g. after an interruption) is waited for. Only the downloads are brought in line with select: removed fields are dropped locally (no requests), added fields re-download the records. Credits are charged per request, not per field, so fetching only the new fields would cost the same.

  • refresh = TRUE: the query is imported again into the same collection, adding works that match it now, and everything is downloaded again. An import only adds: members that no longer match stay.

  • Changed query: the old collection is deleted and a new one is created under the same name (it gets a new ID).

Costs: creating and managing collections and downloading the member IDs are free. An import costs the same credits as paging through the results yourself (one list request per 200 results). Imports run at about 200 results per second (measured November 2026), so a collection of the maximum 1,000,000 members takes over an hour. Interrupting pro_collection() does not stop the import on the server; running it again waits for it.

Limits: 1,000,000 members per collection, 500 collections per account, names up to 100 characters and unique per account. A collection with more than 300,000 members (100,000 for authors) cannot be used as a filter, so its records cannot be downloaded with select; its member IDs can. Queries with group_by or sample cannot be imported.

API key: collections need a personal OpenAlex API key; organisation keys and some older keys are refused (HTTP 401) even when they work for queries.

See also

pro_fetch(), pro_query(), vignette("collections").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
q <- pro_query(search = "coral bleaching", publication_year = 2024)
f <- pro_collection(q, name = "coral bleaching 2024", project_folder = "proj")
id <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(f, "_collection.json"))$collection_id

# Later: records of the collection that are open access
pro_fetch(pro_query(collection = id, is_oa = TRUE), project_folder = "oa")

# Add titles to the download (re-downloads the records)
pro_collection(q, name = "coral bleaching 2024", project_folder = "proj",
               select = c("id", "title"))
} # }
